topics.label: Lecture framing and the cancer hallmarks framework
topics.groupedBecause: This opening establishes the lecture’s aims and introduces the framework used to connect cancer mutations with their functional consequences.

topics.label: Signaling mutations that promote growth and survival
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how mutations in extracellular signaling pathways free cancer cells from normal controls on growth and survival.

topics.label: Disrupted differentiation in blood and intestinal cancers
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics show how altered differentiation shapes cancer cell behavior and tissue organization.

topics.label: Resistance to apoptosis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how changes in the p53-regulated apoptotic machinery allow cancer cells to evade death.

topics.label: Telomere maintenance and cancer cell immortalization
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the telomere-dependent limit on cell division and how cancer cells overcome it by increasing telomerase expression.

topics.label: p53-mediated genome protection and growth-control safeguards
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain p53-dependent safeguards against transformation and conclude the discussion of how mutations undermine normal growth control.

topics.label: Metabolic rewiring in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how altered metabolism supports cancer and interacts with the molecular changes driving it.

topics.label: Angiogenesis in tumor development
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how the angiogenic switch supplies the perfusion needed for tumors to grow.

topics.label: Metastatic spread and successful colonization
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how cancer cells reach distant sites and what determines whether they establish detectable metastases.

topics.label: Lecture conclusions and further reading
topics.groupedBecause: This closing draws together the hallmarks framework, recommends further reading, and ends with questions and practical-session arrangements.
